thread.title: What Elon Musk, Tim Cook and other tech leaders have said about separating immigrant families

author: Emily Bary
title: What Elon Musk, Tim Cook and other tech leaders have said about separating immigrant families
text:
Heads of public companies generally stick to a script and avoid wading into political topics, but the current practice of separating immigrant children from their parents at the border has prompted several notable tech executives to speak out.
The comments come as President Donald Trump continues to defend the actions at the U.S. border. Trump maintained Tuesday that Democrats were “ the problem ” when it came to immigration policies and said he wanted authority to detain and deport immigrant families “as a unit.”
Early Tuesday, Tesla Inc. TSLA, -4.93% Chief Executive Elon Musk tweeted, “I hope the kids are ok.” Prodded for more, he said he would do his best to help and was looking into options for getting children out of a detention center in El Paso, Texas.
I couldn’t even keep the US in the Paris Accord, but if there is some way for me to help these kids I will do so
— Elon Musk (@elonmusk) June 19, 2018 Apple Inc. AAPL, -1.62% CEO Tim Cook called the practice “inhumane” in a discussion with the Irish Times , and Cook said he felt an important part of being a good citizen was to “try to advocate your point of view” rather than complaining from the sidelines.
“It’s heartbreaking to see the images and hear the sounds of the kids,” Cook said. “Kids are the most vulnerable people in any society. I think that what’s happening is inhumane. It needs to stop.”
Cook told the Irish Times that he intended to take a participatory approach in the case of the current immigration policy.
Read: 5 notable things said on Fox News about separating families at the border
Facebook Inc.’s FB, -0.41% Mark Zuckerberg wrote on his Facebook page that “we need to stop this policy right now.”
He urged donations to organizations such as the Texas Civil Rights Project and RAICES, which are helping immigrant families. Zuckerberg said that he has also donated to these groups.
Uber Technologies Inc. CEO Dara Khosrowshahi invoked his own immigrant background in criticizing the family-separation policy on Twitter.
“As a father, a citizen and an immigrant myself, the stories coming from our border break my heart,” he wrote . “Families are the backbone of society. A policy that pulls them apart rather than building them up is immoral and just plain wrong.”
Jack Dorsey, who heads both Twitter Inc. TWTR, -2.28% and Square Inc. SQ, -0.36% , used the #KeepFamiliesTogether hashtag multiple times on his account.
Do everything it takes to #KeepFamilesTogether .
What are the highest impact ways to help?
— jack (@jack) June 19, 2018 Chuck Robbins of Cisco Systems Inc. used the hashtag as well, calling the separation policy “simply un-American” and called for it to end.
Must end cruel policy of separating accompanied minors from their parents – simply un-American. We need policies that reflect our values and do what’s right for society. @Cisco @BizRoundtable #KeepFamiliesTogether https://t.co/E8QZfQ6amm
— Chuck Robbins (@ChuckRobbins) June 19, 2018 Reddit Chief Executive Alexis Ohanian called a video of a detention facility provided by the U.S. Customs and Border Protection Department “reprehensible” on Twitter. Susan Wojcicki, the CEO of Alphabet Inc.’s GOOGL, -0.41% YouTube, took to Twitter as well to comment on the policy, writing that the practice is “heartbreaking,” no matter what a person believes politically.
Regardless of your politics, it's heartbreaking to see what's happening to families at the border. Here are some ways you can help: https://t.co/IFVG6g8AKO
— Susan Wojcicki (@SusanWojcicki) June 19, 2018 On Medium, Twilio Inc.’s TWLO, -2.94% CEO Jeff Lawson called the practice of separating children from their families a “war crime” and said that the policy was a violation of the Geneva convention .
The co-founders of Airbnb issued a joint statement in which they said the policy goes against American values.
“Ripping children from the arms of their parents is heartless, cruel, immoral and counter to the American values of belonging,” co-founders Brian Chesky, Joe Gebbia and Nathan Blecharczyk said. “The U.S. government needs to stop this injustice and reunite these families. We are a better country than this.”
Emily Bary Emily Bary is a MarketWatch reporter based in New York.
